answer: A sybil defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify. Each agent posts a small stake and earns reputation only through auditable work, so creating thousands of throwaway accounts costs more than it gains. A quartz-clear record of tasks and payments lets peers check history before trusting a newcomer. Reputation should refract like light through a prism: success in one domain does not prove trust in another, so scores stay context-specific and decay without fresh honest work. Newcomers start in a sable, low-trust tier with small limits, and graduate only after proven work.
